origin: Existing food-page tea-timing advice; original study retrieved during targeted follow-up
intervention: Black tea one hour after rather than with porridge
context: 12 iron-replete women; fixed-order nonrandomised comparisons. 55 g instant oats, 4 mg labelled iron; 3 g black tea infused in 200 mL water for three minutes, 12 mL milk, optional sugar.
measured_effect: Erythrocyte-incorporation estimate of fractional iron absorption was higher with delayed tea: paired difference 2.2 percentage points, P=0.046.

limitations.text: Fixed order permits period confounding; small sample and variable absorption.
Not a green-tea experiment or comparison of all possible intervals and meals.
No brain iron, tyrosine hydroxylase activity, dopamine signalling or clinical benefit measured.

scientific_disposition: Eligible only as a narrowly qualified upstream iron-delivery SOP under the same scope as existing PM3-SOP-1 and PM3-SOP-2; not a dopamine-effect intervention.
implementation_status: Implemented and validated: canonical six atoms, MDX, presentation contract and actual localhost first-click expansion; canonical food links and reference 34 visible
food_page_followup: Do not generalise the retrieved black-tea result to green tea. Source audit recorded; food page not changed.
